diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: A citizen in Ahvaz says the electricity in their area is cut off three times a day. He attributes this situation to the actions of the Islamic Republic. The reason for these outages is unclear.

Mohammad Jafar Ghaem Panah, the executive deputy of Pezeshkian, spoke about the economic situation and inflation in Iran. He said inflation ranges from 30 to 80 percent and food inflation is 123 percent. He also mentioned budget problems and the impact of war on inflation.

The Iranian women's national football team camp will be held from September 2 to 8 at the National Football Center to produce a documentary about the players' return from Australia. The camp has faced protests from league coaches. Farideh Shojaei stated that the main goal is to film the documentary and players will not be pressured with football training.

Ruhollah Rahimpour said the likelihood of renewed clashes has increased after US attacks on IRGC positions on Larak Island, but a full-scale war is unlikely. He added that the US has shifted its tactics to preventive actions to avoid blocking the Strait of Hormuz.

Morteza Kazemian described the IRGC attacks on the UAE and Jordan as mostly propagandistic and performative. He stated that the US continues to deliver precise and controlled strikes against the Islamic Republic. If American forces are killed, the cycle may get out of control and lead to a new phase of war.

Reza Goharzad discussed the new secondary US sanctions and pressure on Egypt Bank branches in the UAE to isolate Iran economically. He said economic pressure alone will not lead to the overthrow of the Islamic Republic. The overthrow will ultimately be by the Iranian people through protests.

Fatemeh Mohitizadeh broke the national heptathlon record with 5813 points at the women's national athletics championship in Shiraz. She has improved the record three times in less than a year. This achievement makes her one of Iran's main hopes in athletics for the Nagoya Asian Games.

Manshe Amir, a Middle East expert, said that although it is not possible to discuss Israel's practical plans regarding Netanyahu's emphasis on overthrowing the Islamic Republic, Israel has shown initiative in the past. He added that Israel has plans and capabilities to facilitate a popular uprising in Iran and can implement them if necessary.

A citizen sent a video showing darkness in Mahestan city in Alborz province. He says there is no electricity in the morning and power outages occur at night. This highlights electricity problems in the area.

Mehdi Torabi, the national winger of Tractor, has suffered a severe injury to his cruciate ligament during team training. Initial examinations have increased concerns about a ligament tear, and doctors will perform additional MRIs for final confirmation. If confirmed, Torabi will face a long absence from the field and will miss the 2027 Asian Cup.

The death sentence of Ali Asghar Peygambari, a detainee from the December 2025 protests, was confirmed by the Supreme Court. He was recently transferred from Tehran Grand Prison to Qezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. This transfer has caused concern for his family.

Hossein Aghaei stated that a new round of US attacks in Larak occurred in response to the Islamic Republic's efforts to escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. The continuation of these attacks depends on Tehran's subsequent actions.

Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei stated that the enemy and their agents are planning anti-security actions in Iran. He warned that a strong response will be given if unrest occurs. Security forces and the judiciary are at the highest level of readiness.

Messages and videos report long queues and closure of some fuel stations in various cities in Iran. Access to gasoline has become difficult, and queues continue even at midnight. This issue is discussed in an interview with Leila Saadati.

The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs reserves the right to respond to recent drone attacks by the Islamic Republic according to international law. These attacks are described as violations of sovereignty and threats to UAE security. The UAE holds the Islamic Republic fully responsible for these attacks and their consequences.

The 107th Tehran derby will be held on Wednesday, 11 Shahrivar, at the Naqsh-e Jahan Stadium in Isfahan. Despite the stadium's 75,000 capacity, only 35,000 tickets have been offered, with 29,000 for men and 6,000 for women. The ticket share for Esteghlal and Persepolis is equally divided.

Mani Safarpour, an 18-year-old from Lahijan, was killed by government agents with gunfire in Sarsabil, Tehran on January 8, 2026. A video shows his mother's distress while arranging his clothes. This incident was reported to Iran International.

The deputy of food and drug at Shiraz University of Medical Sciences reported a complete shortage of about 40 types of medicines needed by special and cancer patients. A significant part of this shortage involves imported and expensive drugs. Currency transfer issues, sanctions, and lengthy import processes are factors contributing to this situation.
A citizen sent a video showing a dark road at night. He says the road lights are off and the lane markings are inadequate. Drivers have to take risks while driving on this road.

The first strategic political and defense committee meeting of the Makkah Defense Pact will be held on Tuesday in Istanbul. Officials from Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia will participate in the meeting. It is expected that the framework for establishing a secretariat and mechanisms for future cooperation will be determined.

Asaad Salehi, a board member of the Supreme Association of Workers' Trade Unions, called for updating wages due to the sharp decline in workers' purchasing power. He rejected claims that wage increases cause inflation and described the allocation of ration cards as shirking legal responsibility. Salehi emphasized that workers' household expenses can only be met through a real increase in purchasing power.

Kayhan newspaper accused the government media section of leaking a video of an internal government meeting, calling it 'feeding the enemy.' Kayhan also accused appeasers of retreating from enrichment and missile programs. This reaction followed the release of Masoud Pezeshkian's criticism of the IRIB.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated in a meeting with the Indian Prime Minister that the Islamic Republic has adhered to its commitments under agreements, but the US has not fulfilled its obligations. He emphasized efforts to achieve a path of agreement and understanding and said the continuation of war benefits no one. He also highlighted India's significant capacity to help strengthen peace and stability in the region.

In an Instagram poll by Iran International, over 44% of respondents said that despite having financial means, they are unwilling to invest in or buy property in Iran due to the country's unstable conditions. The poll was conducted on Instagram. More details are available in an interview with Seba Heydarkhani.

The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that it reserves the full and legitimate right to respond to recent drone attacks by the Islamic Republic in accordance with international law. This statement was issued on Monday, 9th of Shahrivar. An Iran International reporter covers reactions to the Islamic Republic's attacks in the region.

A citizen from Shiraz reported that fuel stations announce the end of their fuel card quota after a few hours. Then they sell gasoline at a higher price. This issue was sent to Iran International in a video.

On the evening of Sunday, 8 Shahrivar 1405, the US army targeted two IRGC launchers on Larak Island. The IRGC confirmed casualties among its forces and local residents. The governor of Qeshm stated that two people were killed and one wounded in the attack.

Hamidreza Hajibabaei, the deputy speaker of the parliament, stated that any country exporting oil to reduce international pressure on the US should be attacked. He also said that anyone aiding the US should be targeted and that the Islamic Republic should surround the US in the region. Hajibabaei emphasized that they have dealt and will deal multiple times the damage to the US in military attacks.

A citizen reported that the Agriculture Jihad of Mashhad has not provided tractor fuel quotas for six months and has only paid one-third of the wheat payments. Additionally, they do not supply diesel and water is cut off for six hours a day. The Agriculture Jihad office in Mashhad has closed its main doors, and employees enter through the back door and parking lot.

Saeed Golsorkhi, a 31-year-old athlete from Shahroud, was killed during a security forces raid on his home after being injured in the National Iranian Revolution in January. He died in his mother's arms and in front of his young nephew. More details are provided in an interview with Farnoush Faraji.
Ebrahim Rahmanpour, a citizen from Naqadeh, was sentenced by the judicial authority to 38 months and 15 days of imprisonment.

Reports indicate that in the suburban areas of Gorgan, water is available only 8 hours a day and was completely cut off on Sunday. People complain about fuel shortages and frequent power outages in villages. Additionally, hijab enforcers have returned and coercive measures have started gradually in cities.

The Minister of Education announced that more than 15,000 students with special needs have been left out of education. This statistic pertains to the country's special education sector. This issue raises concerns about access to education for these students.

The price of the US dollar in Iran surpassed 210,000 tomans on Monday, 9th of Shahrivar. The British pound also exceeded 284,000 tomans and the euro reached around 243,000 tomans. The price of each new design gold coin also exceeded 223 million tomans.

The Hana Human Rights Organization reported that at least 77 Kurdish citizens in cities and villages of Kurdistan have been arrested by security agencies. Most of these arrests were made without summons or judicial orders. Three detainees were sentenced to 74 lashes and one received a death sentence.

Thirteen citizens from Qorveh were sentenced to a total of 24 years, three months, and one day in prison by Branch 102 of the criminal court. Four of them were also sentenced to a total of 196 lashes, and one was sentenced to two years of exile in Minab. These sentences are related to the December protests.

Donald Trump announced that the United States will respond tonight to Iran's missile attack on American forces. He emphasized that a hard strike will be delivered to Iran. Trump said there will be a response.

Abolfazl Shekarchi, senior spokesperson of the armed forces, described the US army as a Hollywood and promotional army. He said their greatest pride is revealing the weakness and lack of morale of the US and Israeli armies. According to him, the whole world has understood this.

Four citizens from Zahedan arrested during the 1401 nationwide protests were sentenced to prison by the Zahedan Criminal Court. Hamidreza Kouhkan, Ahmadali Kouhkan, and Mohammad Khrot Dinmohammadi each received five years in prison, while Khaled Kashani was sentenced to two years and one day, with his sentence suspended. Khaled Kashani's sentence has been suspended.

Hakan Fidan, Turkey's foreign minister, described Netanyahu as a major threat to the region and the international community. He called the Israeli prime minister a criminal and said he must be stopped. These remarks were made at the Political and Defense Committee meeting of the Mecca Pact in Istanbul.

Masoud Pezeshkian and Abbas Araghchi participated in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Kyrgyzstan. Pezeshkian will meet with regional officials on the sidelines of the summit. Presidents of Turkey, Russia, and China, as well as prime ministers of India and Pakistan, are also attending the summit.

CENTCOM stated that no ship in the Strait of Hormuz has hit a mine. The command rejected the IRGC's claim about a supertanker hitting two naval mines and stopping. CENTCOM described this claim as an attempt to intimidate commercial shipping in the region.

The executive deputy of Masoud Pezeshkian stated that the government's financial and currency policies have caused inflation and increased living pressures. Mohammad Jafar Ghaempanah said that due to budget deficits, they are forced to print money, which creates inflation. Economic journalist Ashkan Nezamabadi described this admission as unprecedented but containing misleading points.

Netanyahu claims in Hebrew that he deceived the US government and dragged it into war with Iran on behalf of Israel. He laughs and says he influenced the US through 1000 hours of appearances on American TV networks. However, in English, he praises the leadership of the US president.

Donald Trump called Iran a failed state and described its economic and military situation as collapsed. He claimed that Iran's leaders should be tried for war crimes against humanity. Trump also referred to the suppression of internal protests and the killing of over 100,000 people.

The European Union announced on Monday that it will continue cooperation with the US and international partners to maintain pressure on Iran. The EU welcomed efforts to stop Iran's destabilizing activities and engage in peace talks, including through further economic pressure such as the US-led economic exclusion operation. The statement was issued ahead of the G20 meeting.

The head of the judiciary of the Islamic Republic threatened to deal more decisively with elements that disrupt the country's security. This threat came following the worsening economic crisis and the rise of the dollar to 210,000 tomans. Additionally, Fars news agency demanded a firm response from the Ministry of Science and security agencies regarding the presence of female students without mandatory hijab in a meeting.

Hossein Ziyari, a football referee and director general of planning and budget in Semnan province, has been sentenced to 5 years in prison. He was arrested on May 3rd by security forces and subjected to physical abuse. His charges include connections with opposition groups and individuals such as Mohammad Reza Faghani.

A senior Iranian source told Reuters that in response to any US attack, the Islamic Republic will give a response dozens of times larger. He said the retaliatory response to US attacks showed that no target in the region is beyond Tehran's reach and conditions in the Strait of Hormuz will worsen for vessels violating Tehran's rules. The source described the recent clashes as a limited and contained confrontation between Tehran and Washington.

Bradley Barcola transferred from Paris Saint-Germain to Liverpool with a 123 million pound contract. He signed a five-year deal and will wear the number 29 jersey. Barcola stated his goal is to win the English Premier League.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, stated that Washington will continue economic pressure on the Islamic Republic. These remarks were made on the sidelines of the G20 meeting in North Carolina. More details were provided in an interview with Maryam Rahmati.

The Secretary-General of the Nurses' House reported a shortage of at least 100,000 nursing staff in the country and said about 60 to 70 thousand nurses have become inactive. Low salaries and poor working conditions have caused nurses to leave the profession. The head of the Nursing Organization also stated that the recruitment of nurses in the public sector is less than the number trained annually.

Rich McCormick, a US congressman, called the Iranian government untrustworthy and accused it of targeting Americans and fueling terrorism. He called for a decisive end to the war. He also emphasized the need to prevent the Islamic Republic from threatening the American people again.

The cancellation of international English language exams has become a new concern for applicants seeking educational migration. This issue is raised alongside economic migration problems. More details are provided in an interview with Baharan Azadi.

Al Hilal club in Saudi Arabia mutually terminated Karim Benzema's contract. Benzema scored 10 goals and made 5 assists in less than a year at Al Hilal. He does not intend to retire and has received offers including from the MLS.

Employees of Aryan Steel Company in Qazvin protested on Tuesday, September 9, due to power outages and factory closure. The factory's electricity has been completely cut off for about five months. Production activities in this facility have stopped.

Tasnim news agency reported that one of the injured in the US attack on Larak Island died from severe injuries. The death toll from this attack reached three. The attack occurred on Sunday night and the injured were taken to the hospital.

Job seekers in Gachsaran protested against the hiring process at the newly opened Lishter refinery. Security forces fired shots to disperse the protesters. Reports indicate that one person was injured during the shooting.

Mohammad Reza Naqdi stated that over 90% of the Islamic Republic's missile reserves remain intact and the missile production network is stable and self-sufficient. He said the Islamic Republic is fulfilling the Supreme National Security Council's commitments but will respond heavily if attacked. Naqdi also mentioned that so far the conflict has been conventional and they have not yet entered asymmetric warfare.

Retired telecommunications workers held protest gatherings in Isfahan, Shiraz, Sanandaj, and Arak. They demand the implementation of the third phase of salary adjustment and the 89/24 employment regulation. Addressing supplementary insurance issues is also among their demands.

Iran International has revealed the identities of members of the IRGC Intelligence Unit 4000. This unit has recruited three individuals through clerics from Thailand and Indonesia for sabotage in East Asian waters. The report was prepared by Mojtaba Pourmohsen.

Lionel Messi announced that after some reflection and an incident involving his father, he has decided to retire from the Argentina national team. He wrote in a note that the decision is painful but the time has come. Messi emphasized that he always gave his best for the national team.

The police commander of Rudsar announced the arrest of a 29-year-old citizen in the city. The individual is accused of causing public disturbance on social media. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Donald Trump posted an animation of the bombing of Khark Island on Truth Social. JD Vance described this action as a message to the Iranian government. Trump does not disclose military actions on social media.

Hamid Ghanbari, Deputy Foreign Minister, stated that the new US sanctions will not change the policies of the Islamic Republic. He added that the enemy seeks media pressure and exaggeration about the effects of the sanctions.

Alireza Elhami, commander of the air defense joint headquarters, stated that the Islamic Republic is a decisive victor in the battlefield. He mentioned that information about scientific and defense achievements is less published to be better utilized. These remarks were made at a ceremony at the burial site of Ruhollah Khomeini.

Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan have agreed to establish a secretariat for the Makkah Joint Defense Pact in Saudi Arabia. Pakistan will lead the secretariat for the first three years. Turkey is also considering mechanisms for other countries to join the pact.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, expressed concern about vulnerabilities caused by ongoing US operations in Iran. He stated that the military has not been sufficiently funded for years. Earlier, senior US military officials warned about the instability of the Iran war.
Employees of Aryan Foolad Qazvin protested due to five months of power outage and unemployment. They stated they have not received any wages during this period. The protest took place today.

Arzoo Karimi stated that the sharp increase in rent has pushed more groups, including employees and the middle class, to the outskirts of cities. This trend has forced families to cut costs on education, healthcare, and nutrition. It also leads to increased inequality and social harm.

The name of Lake Ontario was suddenly changed to Lake America on some online Google maps. This change has caused new disputes between Canada and the United States. Canadian officials have reacted strongly to this action.
A citizen reported that their electricity bill for one month was about one million tomans. This was reported via a voice message to Iran International.

Leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization member countries gathered in Bishkek on Monday, September 9. Vladimir Putin and Narendra Modi discussed the Ukraine war, and Putin met with Xi Jinping. Additionally, Masoud Pezeshkian met with Shehbaz Sharif and emphasized expanding bilateral relations.

At least 10 protests were held today, Monday, 9 Shahrivar, in various cities of Iran. The protest of job seekers in Gachsaran escalated into violence due to police gunfire. Additionally, retirees and company employees held protests in several cities.

The Football Federation announced Moud Bonyadifar as the referee for the 107th derby between Esteghlal and Persepolis. The match will take place in the fifth week of the Premier League on September 1, 2026, at the Naqsh-e Jahan Stadium in Isfahan. Alireza Ildarom, Bahman Abdollahi, and Seyed Reza Mahdavi will assist Bonyadifar in this game.

Ynet reported that Israel was informed before the US attack on Larak Island. Israeli officials do not expect the conflict between the Islamic Republic and the US to escalate into a broader confrontation. A US official stated that American forces are monitoring regional developments and remain ready to protect the Strait of Hormuz.

Workers at Kish Choob company, the maintenance unit of railway infrastructure in Dorud, and Simaye Chabahar company reported non-payment of their wage and insurance claims. Health workers at the Qasr-e Qand Health Center also expressed dissatisfaction with unpaid bonuses and delayed payments of their incentives.

The Football Federation has organized a new camp for the women's national team. The purpose of this camp is to record a commissioned documentary for a non-football entity about the players' return from Australia. An interview was conducted with Masoumeh Hasrati, a former Iranian women's national football player.

Reza Alijani attributed recent disagreements between the government and conservatives to a decision-making crisis over negotiations with the US, enrichment, and economic crisis management. Part of the government supports interaction due to economic and security pressures, but hardliners insist on their previous positions. This situation indicates a decision-making crisis at the highest levels of the Islamic Republic.

The General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic stated that it will not tolerate attacks by the US from regional countries on Iranian targets and will respond heavily. The statement said the US military must leave the region. Iranian forces will target the origin of any operation.

A group of Iranians living in the UK held a car caravan protest in the streets of London on Monday, 9th of Shahrivar. They carried the Lion and Sun flags and protested against the Islamic Republic. This event was reported through videos sent to Iran International.
The IRGC has started a new phase of efforts to lay mines in the Hormuz region.

Donald Trump and his advisors are considering limited attacks in the Strait of Hormuz to prevent Iran from rebuilding its radar and missile capabilities. The plan was prepared by the US Central Command and supported by the Secretary of Defense. Trump may approve the plan following increased tensions.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad stated that the Islamic Republic claimed an attack on a supertanker and ships in the Strait of Hormuz, but the US Central Command denied the claim. He added that such claims have been made several times but are not true. According to him, these actions indicate a decline in the military capability of the Islamic Republic.

Abbas Araghchi stated after the Shanghai summit that the US has violated the Islamabad agreement and must return to its commitments. He added that after the US returns, the current situation can be resolved. Masoud Pezeshkian also called for the US to return to this agreement.

At least six death sentences were carried out in prisons in Rasht and Tabriz. Two defendants in Tehran were sentenced to death through the Qasameh ceremony, and one person's sentence was overturned by the Supreme Court. Additionally, a death row prisoner in Tehran was spared execution with the consent of the victim's family.
The IRGC has threatened to bring an asymmetric war to Manhattan and New York. This news was released in the audio version of Titraval with Niusha Sarami. More details are provided in this report.

Mohammadzadeh was removed from the play "Arash" due to "lack of audience interest." Farhikhtegan newspaper suggested a possible link between this decision and Mohammadzadeh's support for Palestine. Despite high ticket prices, audiences had purchased the tickets.

The Iranian Armed Forces Headquarters stated that the US uses the airspace or soil of some Middle Eastern countries to target Iran and warned it would target them. This statement came after Trump's announcement of retaliatory attacks against Iran. Iran threatened to respond more heavily if US attacks continue.

The judiciary announced the pardon, reduction, or conversion of sentences for 2,577 convicts from various courts. It is unclear how many of these are convicts from revolutionary courts. Convicts of security crimes, espionage, and actions against national security will not be pardoned.

On the early morning of Saturday, 7 Shahrivar, Hana Rakan, a 16-year-old girl from Kermanshah, was killed by her father. The incident occurred while she was sleeping. This news was reported by Harana news agency.
In the audio version of the program 24 with Fardad Farahzad, Trump's emphasis on a severe attack on Iran is discussed.

Mohammadreza Zafarghandi, the Minister of Health, attributed the increase in drug prices to inflation in transportation and raw materials and called for insurance to cover these price hikes. He stated that there is no shortage of medicine and efforts are being made to import drugs through other means. He also mentioned the rising costs of aluminum and petrochemical products used in drug packaging.

Farideh Shojaei announced a sudden camp for the women's national football team to complete the visual archive of the Asian Cup matches. The camp aims to record parts that could not be filmed during the competition. The goal is to create a complete and lasting archive of the national team's participation in these matches.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency announced on Monday that it received a report about an incident in the Indian Ocean. The incident involved a tanker and military forces. No further details were provided.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi stated that the US pursues three simultaneous strategies: weakening the military power of the Islamic Republic, increasing economic pressure, and limiting Tehran's energy leverage. He added that part of the Islamic Republic's military capability in the Persian Gulf has been damaged, limiting Tehran's options. Continued tensions could lead to more costly scenarios.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry, responded to the EU statement supporting the US economic war against Iran by saying Europe cannot claim strategic autonomy while acting as Washington's executor. He emphasized that autonomy requires the will and ability to make independent decisions. Baqaei urged Europe to choose between being an independent actor or merely echoing other countries' policies.
The US has carried out attacks. The IRGC's mine-laying project in Hormuz has failed. This topic was discussed in the program Cheshmandaz with Mahdi Mahdavi Azad.

Dmitry Peskov, Kremlin spokesperson, stated that discussing mediation in the Iran war remains difficult. This topic is scheduled to be discussed in the meeting between Vladimir Putin and Masoud Pezeshkian. They will also talk about Moscow-Tehran relations.

Alireza Babaei, CEO of Chadormalu Ardakan club, revealed that the Secretary-General of the Football Federation requested money from clubs under the pretext of helping the national team and rewarding female national team players who intended to seek asylum in Australia. Gol Gohar club paid 100 billion tomans for the national team's dispatch to the federation. The Secretary-General also asked clubs to pay amounts to encourage the female players to return.

Amir Ghalenoei, the head coach of Iran's national football team, attended the training of the national youth team and gave them advice. He called the youth the future of Iranian football. These remarks came while Ghalenoei has been criticized for relying less on young players in the past four years.

Reports indicate that police fired at young protesters in gatherings in Gachsaran and Ahvaz. The protesters demanded transparency in hiring and priority for local workers. Iranian officials have not yet commented on the incident.

Morad Vaisi said Trump has threatened to respond harshly to new attacks by the IRGC on US forces. The IRGC also stated that if targeted again, it will respond strongly. It appears the two sides are moving toward a new conflict, raising the question of whether it will escalate into a war or remain limited.

Donald Trump said that if the Islamic Republic cannot have nuclear weapons, there will be no subject left for negotiation. He considered military action against Iran necessary to prevent threats to the US and instability in the Middle East. Trump also stated that the Islamic Republic no longer holds the position of Middle East bully.

Morad Veysi, a senior analyst at Iran International, stated that 22 death sentences and dozens of heavy prison sentences have been issued for protesters in Isfahan. He described these actions as the Islamic Republic's revenge against the uprising of the people of Isfahan. He characterized this as part of a widespread wave of repression against the people of Iran.
The audio version of the Politics program with Murad Veisi has been released. The topic of the program is the expectation of a limited US attack. This program is presented by Iran International.

JD Vance said Donald Trump has sent a message to the Islamic Republic that Washington is aware of attacks on commercial ships and has the means to counter them. He accused the Islamic Republic of acting like a terrorist state. He warned that if the attacks continue, there will be consequences.

Morad Veysi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said that people this week focused mainly on three problems: gasoline shortage and possible price increase, severe food inflation, and confusion about school reopening and children's education status. These issues have caused widespread concern and reactions.

John Bolton called the oil blockade of Iran a major victory for the United States and said it would have a significant impact on Iran's economy. He also accused China of cooperating with Iran in money laundering financial assets. Bolton said that Trump is unlikely to increase pressure on China before Xi Jinping's visit to Washington.

A video shows a kilometer-long queue of cars at the Pak Gohar fuel station in Saravan. Citizens have been present since early morning to receive their gasoline quota. Due to the long queue, people have to wait for several hours.

The opening ceremony of the sixth World Nomad Games was held on Monday, 9 Shahrivar, in Bishkek. The event featured music groups, local dances, horseback riding, and fireworks. Several world leaders, including the presidents of Iran and Russia, attended the ceremony.

Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the United Nations, said the Iranian regime does not care about its people and is only focused on maintaining control and money. He called for the enforcement of sanctions and action against shell banks and companies to cut off the regime's financial resources. Waltz emphasized that the world must play its part in this effort.

Donald Trump said the Islamic Republic will never acquire nuclear weapons. He warned that these weapons could lead to the destruction of Israel and the Middle East. Trump also said the Islamic Republic officials do not know who their leader is.

Benjamin Netanyahu said that overthrowing the Islamic Republic is one of Israel's goals. He added that the regime is now much weaker than before. Netanyahu emphasized that the defeat of the Islamic Republic is possible.

Ghassan Ashour said that regional countries bear the highest cost of the 'neither war nor peace' situation. This condition has harmed their economy, trade, energy exports, and tourism. Iran and the US use this opportunity to rebuild their strength, but the UAE, Qatar, and Iraq want to end this situation.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Dan Driscoll, the US Secretary of the Army, has submitted his resignation to Donald Trump. His resignation is still under review and has not been accepted by the White House. Tensions with Pete Hegseth, the Secretary of Defense, over the direction of the force and the dismissal of senior army officers have been cited as reasons for the resignation.

The Minister of Roads and Urban Development announced a serious disruption in the country's aviation radar systems. Due to the lack of radar, some flights are being guided mentally. A defense analyst warned that if navigation systems also fail, the risk of flights will significantly increase.

Six months after the start of US and Israeli attacks, Iranian officials have threatened to target oil exports from Persian Gulf countries if the naval blockade and US pressure continue. Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, said that if the blockade continues, Tehran will not allow 'a single drop of oil' to leave the Persian Gulf. Tehran is trying to spread the costs of the conflict among the US, regional countries, and the global economy by expanding the war.

US sanctions have led to the suspension of certain Treasury Department licenses, restricting educational services for Iranians. These restrictions affect international exams, admission processing, and tuition payments. Iranian students are facing new challenges in their education.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported an incident 17 nautical miles east of Khasab in Oman. A tanker was hit by three unidentified projectiles while exiting the Strait of Hormuz. No casualties or environmental damage have been reported so far.

Mehdi Zare announced the occurrence of 9 earthquakes with a magnitude over three in east Tehran since the beginning of this year. He warned that active faults and soft sediments could increase the risk of earthquakes. The Mosha fault and Parchin and Ivanki faults threaten different areas of Tehran.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations announced that a tanker was targeted while passing through the Strait of Hormuz. The incident occurred 31 kilometers east of the Khasab area in Oman. The tanker was hit by three unknown projectiles.

Israel's public broadcaster Kan reported that the country is not satisfied with the Lebanese army's progress in disarming Hezbollah in southern Lebanon. According to a senior US official, Lebanese army officers have opposed the withdrawal of Israeli forces, fearing Hezbollah's return. The US official said they are working with both sides for a future agreement, but the process will take time.

Jack Keane said Iranian leaders believe they can outlast the US and hope Trump will be weaker after the midterm elections. Iran prioritizes preserving its leadership structure and disregards the suffering of its people. Keane predicted Iran will continue or escalate aggressive actions until the elections.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, is seeking international support to increase economic pressure on Iran at the G20 finance ministers' meeting. He announced that another bank will be sanctioned under the 'Economic Exclusion Campaign' this week, and said the US is ready to apply 'financial violence' if necessary. Bessent also reported full EU support and said that regarding sanctions on China for buying Iranian oil, 'all options are on the table.'

David Zini, head of Shin Bet, has secretly traveled to the United States. The purpose of the trip is to meet FBI officials and discuss sensitive issues including settler violence and the return of Netanyahu's son. This is Zini's first foreign trip since assuming his position.

Kayhan newspaper wrote that the government should listen to the concerns of families worried about the spread of unveiled behavior. The newspaper emphasized that preserving Iranian-Islamic culture and confronting unveiled behavior is the government's duty. Kayhan also mentioned some officials' opposition to warnings directed at unveiled individuals.

Amir Hamidi stated that Washington's current strategy is no longer just containment but aims to change the power calculations in Tehran. The US is pursuing three axes: nuclear, military, and economic. The goal is to severely limit the Islamic Republic's ability to threaten American forces and regional security.

Roghayeh Rezaei reported the confirmation and issuance of death sentences for detainees of the December protests. She described this as a sign of the regime's fear of renewed protests. She also emphasized that these sentences are part of an intensified crackdown and creating fear in society.

Six months after the start of the Iran war, its effects continue to impact the global economy. Reduced refinery capacity and restricted traffic in the Strait of Hormuz have increased fuel prices and energy import costs. This situation has increased inflationary pressures, interest rates, debt, and defense spending for governments.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit that if the US returns to its commitments in the Islamabad agreement, the Islamic Republic will reciprocate immediately. He emphasized that sustainable security comes through mutual trust and respect for national sovereignty. Pezeshkian also said regional security depends on opposing force-based approaches.

Ali Dadpay stated that the dollar price has surpassed 210,000 tomans and the devaluation of the rial is no longer temporary. Iran's economy is moving towards a new equilibrium with high inflation and a weaker rial. He cited money printing, goods shortages, and sanctions as factors worsening the crisis and warned that people's purchasing power will decline.

Reza Goharzad stated that the Islamic Republic has long lacked a clear strategy and its only goal is to preserve the regime. He highlighted the role of the Revolutionary Guards in key decision-making. He also examined the impact of the US midterm elections and Trump's policies.

A citizen sent a video showing air pollution caused by the Qazvin power plant on Tuesday, 10 Shahrivar. The video was sent to Iran International. The issue of air pollution in this area has drawn attention.

A citizen in Shiraz reported that the electricity in their area is cut off for four hours a day. This was reported in a video to Iran International. The power outage has caused dissatisfaction in the area.

All 35,000 tickets for the match between Esteghlal and Persepolis at Naqsh-e Jahan Stadium in Isfahan sold out in less than 2 hours. The match will be held on Wednesday, 11 Shahrivar, and tickets are divided equally between fans of the two teams. Despite the stadium's 75,000 capacity, only half of the capacity was made available for ticket sales.

Morteza Kazemian commented on Masoud Pezeshkian's presence at the Shanghai summit. He questioned whether the positions of the head of the Islamic Republic government truly reflect the views of the hard core of power. Kazemian believes that the main power in Iran is held by the military and the IRGC, and Pezeshkian's statements do not accurately depict the political and economic reality.

Fatemeh Mohajerani, the government spokesperson, attributed the increase in the dollar price to 210,000 tomans to US sanctions. She said the government does not deny the economic pressure but is working to preserve employment and people's livelihoods. Mohajerani also criticized the repeated US violations of agreements.

On Monday, September 9, employees of the Pars Oil and Gas Company held protests at various sections and offshore platforms in the South Pars region. They demanded the removal of salary caps, full payment of wages, and correction of minimum wages. They also requested not to merge the oil pension fund with other pension funds and sought attention to their other demands.

David Zini, head of Israel's internal security agency, traveled secretly to Washington. He will discuss sensitive security cases with FBI officials, including threats against Benjamin Netanyahu's son. The trip took place on Saturday evening.

The disciplinary committee of the Football Federation rejected the complaints from Sepahan and Mes Shahrbabak clubs regarding Yaser Asani's presence in Esteghlal. The league organization has not registered any contract termination for Asani, and Esteghlal proved with a FIFA inquiry that Asani is a legal player. Asani's participation in upcoming Esteghlal matches has no legal obstacles.

Ahmad Taj, a resident of Tehran, was sentenced to seven years in prison by Branch 36 of the Tehran Province Court of Appeals. The sentence was announced on Monday, 9 Shahrivar. The lawyer stated that the verdict was issued without considering the defenses of the case's lawyers.

A video sent to Iran International on Tuesday, 10 Shahrivar, shows contaminated and unsafe tap water in Shiraz. The video depicts the water condition in the city. The issue of unsafe water in Shiraz has drawn attention.
